question: Is the air in Ipoh better than KL right now?
name: Claude
answer:
Probably yes, but I can't confirm it for this exact moment. The search tool only returned cached pages, and the two readings are from different days.

- **Ipoh:** IQAir showed a US AQI of 56 (Moderate), with PM2.5 as the main pollutant. That reading was from 10:00 on Oct 13.
- **Kuala Lumpur:** IQAir showed a US AQI of 203 (Very unhealthy), with PM2.5 at 128 µg/m³. That reading was from 13:00 on Oct 17.

Going by those two snapshots, Ipoh was far cleaner. But they're four days apart, so it isn't a fair like-for-like comparison. KL's forecast also dropped to about 104–110 later that night, so its air can change a lot within a day.

For a live comparison, check these pages side by side:
- IQAir: [Ipoh](https://www.iqair.com/air-quality/malaysia/perak/ipoh) and [Kuala Lumpur](https://www.iqair.com/air-quality/malaysia/kuala-lumpur/kuala-lumpur)
- aqicn.org, which uses the same DOE monitoring data
- The Malaysian Department of Environment's APIMS site, which gives the official API readings

Ipoh is usually cleaner than KL because it has less traffic and industry. Haze episodes and open burning can still affect both cities.
